plan.curriculum: English 2.0, Level 5: VC2E5LA02 taking account of differing opinions; VC2E5LA03 the stages of a persuasive text (conclusion); VC2E5LY10 creating sequenced texts for an audience
plan.shape: model, label, echo, draft: the model's last two paragraphs, a quick label of conclusion parts, an echo-the-hook round, then students finish their whole draft, because a finished draft is what Week 5 needs
plan.criticalFeature: a conclusion tells the reader exactly what to do now, in words that echo the opening
decisionPoints: the Which part of the ending? round
the choice check: the strongest call to action
the exit board: a missing call to action written
plan.anchor: Claim it. Prove it. Sell it. The ending sells one last time and asks for action.
plan.catchUp: Behind on the draft? Write the conclusion first today (it is the shortest), then go back to one body paragraph.

studentTools: Big piece plan and the draft so far
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
Point to A, B or C
boardSetup: Answer back: Some people say... However...
Conclusion: 1 restate, 2 sum up, 3 call to action (echo your hook)

slides.notes: Open the session. One line: today you finish your draft, with a final answer and a final ask.
Print the Worksheet for everyone, the Extension for early finishers and the Supported Worksheet for those who need it. Students who are behind write the conclusion first.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to answer the other side and finish with a strong call to action.
successCriteria: I can name the three parts of a conclusion.
I can write a rebuttal paragraph and a conclusion with a clear call to action.
I can make my ending echo my hook.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: By the end of today, your whole draft is done.
SAY: Read the I can lines with me. Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: Naming the parts is where we start.
Writing the rebuttal and the conclusion is today's main goal.
notes.prep: SC1 naming conclusion parts is reachable for all; SC2 rebuttal and conclusion with a call to action is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 echoing the hook is the stretch.

slides.title: Which ending would the director remember?
lines: That is all. Thank you for reading my letter.
Twenty steps a day is no life for a polar bear. Please give them back their hundreds of kilometres.

notes.answer: the second - it echoes the hook and asks for something
beats: SAY: Two endings for my zoo letter.
The last thing a reader reads is what they remember.
ASK: Which ending would the director remember? First or second?
5 sec. Cue: Fingers at your chest, 1 or 2... show me.
EXPECT: 2
ASK: What did the second ending bring back from the start?
15 sec. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: the twenty steps; the hook
SAY: Today: answer the other side, then finish strong.
trap: choosing the first because it's polite.
Fix: ask what will the director do after reading it? Student re-chooses.
notes.prep: Launch reconnects the Session 2 hook and the Week 1 rebuttal. 3 minutes.

slides.meaning: One clear thing you want the reader to do now.
slides.example: Please switch off one light tonight.

notes.answer: one clear thing you want the reader to do now
beats: POINT to the words. SAY: Call to action. Say it with me. Call to action.
SAY: You call your reader to act. One clear thing, now.
Some of you may remember this from your posters.
ASK: What makes Please switch off one light tonight easy to do?
10 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: it's small, it's clear, it says when
trap: a call to action that is too big: save the world.
Fix: ask what would they do tomorrow morning? Student shrinks it.
notes.prep: Retrieved from the Week 3 posters, now in a written conclusion.

slides.title: Watch me answer back and finish
slides.extract: Some people say zoos help children love polar bears. However, wildlife cameras let millions of children watch wild bears without taking a single bear from the ice. Twenty steps a day is no life for a polar bear. Bears need space, cold and a wild home. Please stop bringing new polar bears to your zoo, and put that money into protecting them in the Arctic.
highlights: Please stop bringing new polar bears
slides.source: Model letter, written for this session

notes.answer: rebuttal, then restate, sum up, call to action
beats: POINT to Some people say.
SAY: I name their best reason fairly, then However, and I beat it.
POINT to Twenty steps a day.
SAY: New paragraph. I restate my position, and it echoes my hook.
POINT to space, cold and a wild home.
SAY: I sum up my three reasons in one line. A rule of three.
ASK: Read my call to action with me.
3 sec. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
EXPECT: Please stop bringing new polar bears to your zoo...
trap: a conclusion that adds a brand new reason.
Fix: student moves the new reason into a body paragraph.
notes.stretch: End on a short sentence that lands like a punch.
notes.help: Three lines: I believe... / ..., ... and ... / Please...
notes.prep: The final model paragraphs of the zoo letter. Critical feature: tell the reader exactly what to do, echoing the opening.

slides.title: Which part of the ending?
slides.pivot: ask: does it repeat, list, or ask?
slides.followUp: cold call one student: which words told you?

items.text: Please give us the empty land behind the library by Term 1.
A vegetable garden is exactly what our school needs.
It would feed the canteen, teach science and calm busy minds.
Our playground deserves more than weeds and broken pavers.

say: 1 restate, 2 sum up, 3 call to action.
Same garden letter as Tuesday, now its ending.
trap: calling the restate a call to action because it sounds strong.
Fix: ask does it ask the reader to do something? If not, it's not the action.
notes.stretch: Put the four lines in the best order.
notes.prep: Guided labelling of conclusion parts, mixed order. SC1.

slides.title: Which is the strongest call to action?
slides.prompt: A letter to the principal about hot classrooms

options.text: Thank you very much for reading my letter today.
Please fit fans in the senior rooms before next summer.
Hot classrooms are not good for anybody at all.

notes.answer: B - one clear action, with a when
beats: SAY: Three possible last lines. Which one gets something done?
ASK: Which is the strongest call to action?
10 sec. Cue: voices off, everyone points to A, B or C.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call: what makes B easy to say yes to?
Less -> ask what would the principal do next? for each, re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: B. One thing, the senior rooms, before summer. Easy to say yes to.
trap: pointing to A because letters end with thank you.
Fix: say thank you can come after the call to action, not instead of it.
notes.prep: Decision point before drafting. Under 80% means students write their call to action on a board first for a check.

slides.title: Echo the hook
slides.pivot: underline the hook's key picture, reuse it in the last line
slides.followUp: cold call one board: which words did you echo?

items.text: Hook: Have you ever eaten a tomato straight off the vine?
items.answer: Give us a garden, and every student can taste one.
items.expect: a last line that brings back the tomato

items.text: Hook: Imagine a beach where you can't see the sand for plastic.
items.answer: Let's make sure our beaches stay golden, not grey.
items.expect: a last line that brings back the beach

items.text: Hook: There's a monster under our school, and it eats our lunches.
items.answer: Let's starve the monster: no more wasted lunches.
items.expect: a last line that brings back the monster

items.text: Hook: What if ten extra minutes made every afternoon calmer?
items.answer: Ten minutes. Calmer afternoons. Please say yes.
items.expect: a last line that brings back the ten minutes

say: Write a last line that brings back the hook's picture.
trap: copying the hook word for word.
Fix: student keeps the picture, changes the sentence.
notes.stretch: Make the echo a call to action too.
notes.help: Start with Let's... and reuse one word from the hook.
notes.prep: Guided practice on SC3: echoing the hook. Hooks retrieved from Week 3.

slides.title: Finish your draft
slides.task: Work through your Worksheet, plan your ending, then draft your rebuttal and conclusion in your writing book.

notes.answer: a rebuttal paragraph and a three-part conclusion; a complete draft
beats: POINT to the task.
SAY: Your Week 1 rebuttal might fit here. Upgrade it for your reader.
SAY: Read the task, complete each part, check your work.
Finished? Extension next. Everyone, together, on three.
CONFERENCE with anyone who is two paragraphs behind. Conclusion first.
ASK: Is your whole draft finished?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: most thumbs up by the end
TIME 22 minutes. At 20, everyone reads their ending to a partner.
trap: a conclusion that just stops: That's why zoos are bad.
Fix: student adds Please... with one clear action.
notes.stretch: Extension: three styles of ending, then choose and read aloud.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: picture-clue choices, a first However done, a conclusion frame.
notes.prep: Independent drafting to a finished first draft. Collect books to read before Session 1 of Week 5. SC2 and SC3.

slides.extendedTask: a worksheet ending in a plan, then the drafted rebuttal and conclusion that finish the big piece

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: The library should stay open at lunch. It gives quiet kids a safe place, builds reading and costs nothing extra.
Write the call to action that finishes this conclusion.

notes.answer: e.g. Please open the library every lunchtime from next Monday
beats: SAY: A new conclusion with its last line missing.
ASK: Write the call to action.
45 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: Please + one clear action + when
RECORD who writes another claim instead of an action. Week 5 revision group.
trap: Fix: none now, record the name.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2 on a new conclusion. One board per student.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Read your partner your hook and your last line. Do they echo each other?

notes.answer: open - listen for a picture or word that returns at the end
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can lines together. Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How proud are you of your finished draft?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down. Read those drafts first.
ASK: Read your hook and your last line. Do they echo?
20 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: yes, both have the twenty steps
notes.prep: Self-assessment read beside the exit boards. Every student ends Week 4 with a complete first draft. SC2.

resources.subtitle: Answer the other side. Then tell the reader exactly what to do.

steps: Does it repeat the claim? Restate
Ask for action? Call to action

items.prompt: Label each line: rebuttal, restate, sum up or call to action.
rows: Some say lights are costly. However, one accident costs far more.
It is cheaper, safer and fairer.
Please install lights by next term.
answers: Some say lights are costly. However, one accident costs far more.
It is cheaper, safer and fairer.
Please install lights by next term.

example.prompt: A conclusion with a new reason?
steps: Move new reasons to a body paragraph
example.answer: Conclusions sum up; they never add new reasons.

items.prompt: Crossing letter. Best call to action?
items.explain: One clear action with a when.

items.prompt: Jai's conclusion adds something new. Find the problem and fix it.
work: Bikes are healthy, cheap and clean. Also, bike shops sell cool helmets.
items.answer: The helmets point is new and off-topic. Fix: cut it, then add: Please build a bike path by summer.

example.prompt: Hook: Imagine a playground with no shade.
example.answer: Let's make sure no child plays in a shadeless playground again.

items.prompt: Write a last line that echoes each hook.
rows: What if every lunch left zero rubbish?
The bear paced to the fence and back.
Imagine a river you could swim in again.
answers: What if every lunch left zero rubbish?
Zero rubbish. Every lunch. Let's start Monday.
The bear paced to the fence and back.
No bear should pace a fence forever.
Imagine a river you could swim in again.
Let's make our river swimmable again.

steps: Their best reason, and my However
Call to action that echoes the hook
example.answer: Some say zoos teach kids. However, cameras do too. ... Please fund wild bears instead.

items.prompt: Plan your rebuttal and conclusion. Then draft them in your writing book.

resources.tip: Finished your draft? Grab the Extension.

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option: three styles of ending, then a final read-aloud check.
resources.title: The Last Word
resources.subtitle: The ending is what readers remember.

example.answer: Question: Would you trade the Arctic for a cage? Picture: ... Punch: Set them free.

items.prompt: Write three different last lines for your own piece.
rows: a picture that echoes the hook
answers: a question the reader keeps answering
a picture that echoes the hook

example.answer: The picture ending: my reader saw the bear at the start, so it brings them full circle.

items.prompt: Which ending will you use? Explain why it suits your reader. Then read your whole draft aloud and fix two things you stumble on.
items.answer: A choice with a reader-linked reason, and two named fixes.

resources.title: Ending Helper
resources.subtitle: Some people say... However... Please...

items.hint: Does it say what to do?

example.answer: Some people say zoos are fun. However, bears need space.

items.hint: The first one is done for you.

example.answer: I believe zoos should not keep bears. They need space, cold and freedom. Please fund wild bears.

items.prompt: Write your conclusion: I believe ___. (three reasons in one line) Please ___.
items.answer: A restated claim, a summary and a call to action.
items.hint: Use the three reasons from your plan.
